title: Data Consistency Models
description: Understand strong vs eventual consistency and CAP theorem.

data.text: Data consistency models define how up-to-date data is across services. Strong consistency is expensive; eventual consistency is scalable.

terms.definition: All reads see the latest write.
Reads will eventually see the latest write.
A distributed system can provide only two of: Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.
The strongest consistency model, where operations appear instantaneous.

data.text: The CAP theorem states that a distributed system can provide only two of three guarantees: Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance. During a network partition, you must choose between consistency and availability.

items: CP systems: sacrifice availability during partition (e.g., HBase)
AP systems: sacrifice consistency during partition (e.g., Cassandra)
CA systems: only in single-node, not distributed

data.text: PACELC extends CAP: if there is a Partition (P), choose Availability (A) or Consistency (C); Else (E), choose Latency (L) or Consistency (C).

items.question: What is the CAP theorem?
items.answer: A distributed system can provide only two of Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance.

items.question: Is eventual consistency bad?
items.answer: No. It is a valid choice for many scenarios where availability matters more than immediate consistency.

items.question: What is PACELC?
items.answer: An extension of CAP that also considers latency when there is no partition.

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Choose consistency model based on business requirements and trade-offs.
